details:
LUNARIS — Lunar Mission Planning and Visualization Platform

Introduction

LUNARIS is a web-based lunar mission planning platform developed by Team CodexGalaxy, Computer Science and Engineering students from IUBAT, Dhaka, Bangladesh, for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026.

Our project addresses the Lunar Landing Site Navigator challenge, which focuses on helping users compare lunar landing sites and mission dates by understanding sunlight conditions and direct-to-Earth communication opportunities.

The Problem

Landing on the Moon requires careful planning. The lunar south pole presents particular difficulties because of low solar elevation angles, complex terrain, long shadows, and changing Earth visibility.

A landing site that appears suitable at one time may become less favorable on another date. These changes can affect potential solar-power generation, communication availability, and scientific operations.

NASA and its partners provide valuable scientific resources, but using several separate tools to evaluate different mission scenarios can be challenging for non-specialists.

Our Solution and Working Process

We developed LUNARIS to bring lunar exploration and mission analysis into a single interactive website.

Step 1 — Select a Landing Site

Users explore an interactive 3D Moon and choose from sixteen predefined locations, including historical Apollo missions, international lunar missions, and clearly labeled south-polar reference locations.

They can also enter custom latitude and longitude coordinates. When a location is selected, the Moon automatically rotates to center the selected position.

Step 2 — Configure the Mission

Users choose their mission start date and duration. These inputs define the time period used for the analysis.

Step 3 — Analyze Sunlight and Earth Visibility

LUNARIS estimates the positions of the Sun and Earth relative to the selected lunar location. The application presents solar elevation, potential sunlight availability, Earth visibility, and periods when both conditions overlap.

Animated timelines help users understand how these conditions change during the mission.

Step 4 — Explore Power Conditions

A simplified solar-power and battery model demonstrates how illumination could influence the energy available for lunar surface operations.

Step 5 — Compare Four Mission Scenarios

Users can compare up to four combinations of landing locations and mission dates. The comparison dashboard displays estimated visibility conditions and exploratory scores, helping users understand trade-offs between scenarios.

Step 6 — Explore Mission Windows

Our exploratory mission-window finder searches alternative dates and ranks them according to the platform's simplified visibility-based scoring model.

Step 7 — Generate a Report

The final page summarizes the selected mission and its estimated conditions. Users can download reports, export comparison information, or print their results.

NASA Data and Scientific Resources

LUNARIS uses NASA lunar mission information and published landing-site coordinates as scientific references.

We studied the NASA/JPL Horizons System for Sun and Earth ephemeris calculations, LROC QuickMap for lunar imagery and mapping, and NASA Moon Trek for lunar exploration and terrain visualization.

Our website currently uses simplified analytical calculations by default. It also provides an optional workflow for importing JPL Horizons ephemeris data.

Measured LOLA elevation data have not yet been integrated, so terrain obstruction and power calculations remain illustrative. The application clearly identifies these limitations.

Technology Stack

We developed the website using HTML, CSS, JavaScript, native WebGL, and browser-based visualization techniques.

GitHub is used for source-code management, while GitHub Pages hosts the public website. The project also includes an optional Python utility for retrieving JPL Horizons information.

ChatGPT assisted with coding, interface development, debugging, and documentation.

Our Innovation

The main innovation of LUNARIS is combining several lunar mission-planning activities into one guided experience.

Instead of simply displaying lunar maps, our platform allows users to select locations, configure dates, examine modeled visibility conditions, compare four scenarios, explore alternative windows, and export the results.

The automatically rotating 3D Moon makes location selection easier to understand, while the visualization and comparison tools help demonstrate how mission conditions can change between sites and dates.

Impact and Future Development

LUNARIS aims to make lunar mission planning concepts more accessible to students, educators, researchers, and space enthusiasts.

Our current version is an educational demonstration rather than a flight-validated engineering tool.

Future improvements include integrating verified JPL Horizons calculations across more locations and dates, processing actual lunar elevation datasets, improving terrain-aware horizon calculations, and developing more advanced mission optimization capabilities.

Through LUNARIS, we hope to help people explore the engineering challenges of future lunar missions while making complex scientific information easier to visualize and understand.

LUNARIS — Plan. Optimize. Simulate.

Team CodexGalaxy
International University of Business Agriculture and Technology (IUBAT)
Dhaka, Bangladesh
